description: Header, nav bar and top utility bar. On a trade site it has to show the phone number and the main action (call / book / estimate) at all times, and can carry hours, service area and licence or audience switches without crowding the logo.
queries: website header with top utility bar showing phone number and hours
restaurant website header with location and opening hours
navigation bar with phone number and call now button

references.layout: No bar or borders. Three items sit on the hero color: 'MENU' top-left, a lowercase serif wordmark centered, 'BOOK A TABLE' top-right. Further down, the hero flanks carry live info on one baseline: 'OPEN TODAY TIL 1:30PM' on the left and 'NEWCASTLE 28°C' on the right, either side of a line illustration with curved text.
references.type: Sans small caps ~11px, tracked ~+8%. Serif lowercase wordmark ~22px. Flank labels match the nav labels exactly.
references.color: Terracotta ~#B9412A background, cream ~#F6E7D7 type, oxblood ~#6E1E14 line illustration.
details: Live hours ('open today til…') and city/weather treated as nav-level information
Only three nav items; the full menu hides behind 'MENU'
Hours and location mirror the nav corners, so the layout feels symmetrical and intentional
references.why_it_works: It shows hours and location can be the most elegant thing on the page instead of a gray utility strip.
references.trade_adaptation: 'MENU · [logo] · BOOK A VISIT', with flanks 'ON CALL TODAY TIL 8PM' / 'SERVING SPOKANE VALLEY'. Swap weather for 'Lic. #EL-20418'.

references.layout: A thin black strip (~18px) with a tiny centered offer line. Below it a nav row ruled top and bottom with ~1.5px black lines: three big links left, the mascot logo centered, three big links right. The hero continues on the same yellow.
references.type: Grotesk caps, regular, ~16px, generous letter and word spacing. The strip text is ~9px caps.
references.color: Yellow ~#FFE94A, black ~#111111 rules and type, black strip with white text.
details: Rules above and below the nav make it read like a newspaper masthead
Links are large enough to work as a design element
Symmetrical 3 + logo + 3 composition
references.why_it_works: Big, confident links and printed-style rules give strong brand presence with no logo bar or shadows.
references.trade_adaptation: Painter or landscaper: 'SERVICES · ABOUT · AREAS · [logo] · REVIEWS · FAQ · CALL', strip 'Free estimates within 48 hours'.

references.layout: A yellow utility bar (~22px) with three slots: tagline left, offer center, language right. Below it a white nav (~36px): square logo left, two link groups (services cluster left-center, projects/segments centered), 'About Us / Contact' and a square-cornered filled tan 'Book a meeting' button right.
references.color: Utility yellow ~#FFE000, white bar, ink ~#111111, tan button ~#C8C1AD.
details: The three-slot utility bar works like a mini information architecture
Links are grouped by intent with real gaps between the groups
The button has zero radius, matching the industrial brand
references.why_it_works: The utility bar carries the hook (price, credentials) so the main nav can stay calm.
references.trade_adaptation: Utility bar: 'Licensed & insured · Lic #12345' | 'Spring AC tune-up $89' | '(555) 012-3456'. Nav button 'Book a visit'.

references.layout: A light gray utility bar (~18px) with right-aligned secondary links. Below it a white nav: logo left, then a location selector right beside the logo (pin icon + 'New York / Tri-State Area ▾'); right side holds a filled 'Sign up', an outline 'Sign in' and a search icon. A breadcrumb row follows.
references.type: Sans ~12-13px. Location selector in medium weight with a chevron.
references.color: Gray ~#F1F1F1 utility bar, white nav, teal button ~#2E7D9A, brand red ~#DA3743.
details: The location selector next to the logo turns geography into navigation
Utility bar holds audience links ('For Businesses')
The main bar stays minimal
references.why_it_works: A location chip beside the logo is the clearest way to say 'we serve your area' and it scales to multi-city operators.
references.trade_adaptation: '📍 Serving: Greater Denver ▾' beside the logo (opens a service-area list). Utility bar: 'For contractors · Careers · Financing'.

references.layout: Tiny audience tabs above the nav ('For shoppers' bold and active, 'For business' gray). The nav row has a wordmark left, 3 links, and on the right a round search icon and a black pill 'Sign in' with a person icon.
references.type: Sans ~11-12px for the tabs (active one bold), ~13px for links. Bold wordmark.
details: The audience switch is tabs, not a dropdown
The pill CTA carries a small icon
Very light chrome above a dark hero
references.why_it_works: It splits two audiences cleanly without adding a menu.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Residential | Commercial' tabs above the nav for electricians, cleaners and pest control, each switching services and the CTA ('Book a visit' vs 'Request a site survey').

references.layout: A dark translucent full-radius pill (~90% width, ~36px tall) floats over an inset hero image that itself has ~16px radius. Links left, wordmark centered, 'Login' text and an orange pill CTA right.
references.color: Pill ~rgba(10,20,25,0.85), white text, orange CTA ~#FF5A1F against a teal-blue photo.
details: Centered wordmark inside the pill
The hero is inset with rounded corners, so the pill reads as an object on a card
One saturated color (the CTA)
references.why_it_works: The pill stays legible over any photo and gives a premium, app-like frame.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Services · Reviews · Areas · About | [logo] | (555) 012-3456 · [Book now]' over a rounded job-site hero.

references.layout: A blocky white wordmark sits free top-left on a full-bleed solar-field photo. A right-aligned dark-gray translucent pill holds 4 links and a nested white 'CONTACT' chip. Nothing else is in the header.
references.type: Sans ~10px for links, chip label in caps.
references.color: Pill ~rgba(60,60,60,0.7), white chip, ochre/brown landscape photo.
details: The CTA is nested inside the pill as a white chip
The logo stays outside the pill, so there are two separate anchors
Compact footprint keeps the landscape dominant
references.why_it_works: It is compact, clearly hierarchical and lets industrial photography breathe.
references.trade_adaptation: Solar or roofing: logo left on the photo, pill 'Services · Projects · About · [CALL NOW]'.

references.layout: Two separate white rounded rectangles float on a green background. The wide one holds logo, links and a green circular menu button. The small one, to its right, holds 'Get a quote' and a round avatar of a real person.
references.color: White pills, green ~#7ED957 background and menu dot, ink ~#222222.
details: The CTA gets its own pill with a human face
The gap between pills separates browsing from acting
The hamburger is a colored circle, not three gray lines
references.why_it_works: A face on the quote button says a real person will answer, which matters for service businesses.
references.trade_adaptation: Quote pill with the owner's headshot: 'Talk to Mike' or 'Get a quote from Dana', next to the main nav pill.

references.layout: Two white rounded cards float at the top corners of a full-bleed sky photo. The left card holds logo and 3 dropdown links; the right card holds 'Pricing', language, an outline 'Login' and a black pill 'Book demo'. The center stays open to the photo.
references.color: White cards, black pill, deep blue dusk sky with warm rock.
details: Split cards leave the center of the photo free for the headline
Browse on the left, act on the right
Small radius (~6px) on the cards, full radius on the buttons
references.why_it_works: Clear separation of intents, and it never covers the subject of the photo.
references.trade_adaptation: Left 'Logo · Services · Areas · About', right '(555) 012-3456 · [Free estimate]' over a landscape or exterior photo.

references.layout: No bar. Links float directly on a full-bleed warm interior photo. A primary group ('Shop Collections Showroom', ~13px) sits center-left; a secondary group ('Info Trade Search', ~10px) sits center-right; 'Sign In Cart (0)' at the far right. The brand name is small, mid-left inside the photo, with a tiny tagline bottom-left.
references.type: Sans medium, white. Two sizes signal hierarchy (~13px primary, ~10px secondary).
references.color: White text on a warm wood and cream photo (~#C9A57A, ~#E8DCC8).
details: Link size, not color or weight, carries the hierarchy
The logo leaves the top-left corner and lives in the composition
The photo is chosen with a calm top band so white text reads
references.why_it_works: It is photography-first. The nav steps back like a gallery caption.
references.trade_adaptation: High-end remodeler or cabinetmaker: 'Kitchens Baths Additions' as the primary group, 'Process Reviews Contact' as the secondary group, over a finished-kitchen photo.

references.layout: A thin bar on a warm gray background: small caps name left, comma-separated nav words centered ('Furniture, Index, Studio'), and 'LOS ANGELES, CA 03:12 ●' right with a live clock and dot. A giant wordmark fills the screen below.
references.type: Grotesk caps ~9px for the corners, ~14px sentence case for the centered nav.
references.color: Warm gray ~#ECE8E1, ink ~#222222, black status dot.
details: The nav is written as a comma-separated phrase, not a row of buttons
City plus live local time signals a real place
Status dot implies 'open now'
references.why_it_works: Minimal and editorial, and the city/clock corner gives local presence for free.
references.trade_adaptation: 'PINE ROOFING · Services, Projects, Contact · BEND, OR 7:42 AM ● OPEN' (dot turns gray after hours, linking to the emergency line).

takeaways: Make phone, hours and service area part of the header system, but style them. Use the nav flanks (Monte), a three-slot utility bar (YLLW) or a city/clock corner (Waka Waka), not a cramped gray strip of icons.
Give the header exactly one primary action, visually distinct (filled pill or chip) and rightmost. Everything else is plain text.
Over photography, float the nav (a full pill, split corner cards, or a pill holding a nested CTA chip) instead of laying a dark gradient across the top.
Put a location selector or 'Serving X' label beside the logo. Local is the selling point.
When a trade has two audiences, use tabs above the nav (Residential | Commercial) rather than a dropdown.
Keep to five links or fewer. Small caps at 11-12px with tracking feel crafted; big caps links with printed rules feel bold.
A human face on the CTA (avatar in the quote pill) signals that a real person answers.
avoid: Mega-menus with icon-and-description dropdown panels (Intercom, Mixpanel, Grammarly). Small businesses have 5-8 pages.
Glassy translucent pills with low contrast over busy imagery (Analogue). They become unreadable.
Three or more competing buttons in the bar (Log in + Sign up + Get a demo + Contact sales).
Default SaaS bar: logo, 5 chevron dropdowns, 'Contact sales', gradient 'Get started' (Linear, Mixpanel, Calendly).
Rainbow or gradient CTA pills and gradient top borders (Speakeasy, Clay).
Hamburger-only navigation on desktop that hides the phone number.
